metaTitle: SIT31021 Cert III in Patisserie RPL — Pastry Chef
metaDescription: Working as a pastry cook? Get the SIT31021 Certificate III in Patisserie through RPL using your kitchen experience. Free eligibility check.
heroIntro: The SIT31021 Certificate III in Patisserie is the trade qualification for pastry cooks. If you already make cakes, pastries, desserts and yeast goods in a commercial kitchen, RPL recognises your experience so you get the qualification without a full apprenticeship.
whoIsItFor:
• Pastry cooks and commis pastry chefs
  • Bakers who specialise in cakes and pastries
  • Cooks who run the dessert section in restaurants or hotels
  • Pastry cooks who trained overseas

You'll usually have two or more years in a commercial kitchen producing cakes, pastries, petits fours, desserts and yeast-based products, while following food safety rules.
evidenceExamples:
• Photos and videos of products you've made: cakes, pastries, desserts, petits fours
  • Recipes, production plans and order sheets you've worked from
  • A reference from your head chef, head pastry chef or employer
  • Food safety and food handler certificates
  • Payslips or a statement of service showing your kitchen roles
description: The SIT31021 Certificate III in Patisserie covers the skills of a qualified pastry cook: producing cakes, specialised cakes, pastries, petits fours, desserts and yeast-based bakery products, using food preparation equipment, basic cookery methods, working effectively in a commercial kitchen, food safety and hygiene, stock control and coaching others.

faqs.q: Can I get a patisserie qualification through RPL?
faqs.a: Yes, if you have worked as a pastry cook. Photos of your products, recipes and a chef's reference are assessed against the units, and practical skills are observed or recorded.

faqs.q: How long does it take?
faqs.a: Usually 6 to 12 weeks, depending on your evidence and practical assessments.

faqs.q: Do I need to do a practical assessment?
faqs.a: Usually yes. An assessor watches you produce a range of products in a commercial kitchen, or reviews recorded video, to confirm your skills.

faqs.q: I trained as a pastry chef overseas. Can my experience count?
faqs.a: Yes. Overseas experience and training can be assessed. Photos, references and any certificates help, and recent Australian kitchen work strengthens your evidence.

faqs.q: What does it cost?
faqs.a: The cost depends on your evidence and any gap training. RPL is usually much cheaper than an apprenticeship. Start with a free eligibility check.

metaTitle: SIT31121 Cert III in Asian Cookery RPL — Fast Track
metaDescription: Experienced Asian cuisine cook? Get the SIT31121 Certificate III in Asian Cookery through RPL using your kitchen experience. Free eligibility check.
heroIntro: The SIT31121 Certificate III in Asian Cookery is the trade qualification for cooks who specialise in Asian cuisine. If you already cook in a commercial Asian kitchen, RPL recognises your experience so you get the qualification without a full apprenticeship.
whoIsItFor:
• Cooks in Chinese, Thai, Vietnamese, Indian, Japanese, Korean, Malaysian or other Asian kitchens
  • Wok and tandoor cooks
  • Restaurant owners who cook in their own kitchen
  • Cooks who trained overseas

You'll usually have two or more years in a commercial kitchen cooking a range of Asian dishes: appetisers, stocks and soups, sauces, salads, rice and noodles, and cooked dishes, while following food safety rules.
evidenceExamples:
• Photos and videos of dishes you cook
  • Menus, recipes and prep lists you work with
  • A reference from your head chef, owner or employer
  • Food safety and food handler certificates
  • Payslips or a statement of service showing your kitchen roles
description:
The SIT31121 Certificate III in Asian Cookery covers the skills of a qualified cook in Asian cuisine: basic Asian cookery methods, preparing appetisers and snacks, stocks and soups, sauces, dips and accompaniments, salads, rice and noodles, and cooked dishes, plus planning and costing menus, preparing food for special diets, food safety, kitchen cleaning, stock control and coaching others.

Electives can focus on particular cuisines. It replaces SIT31116.

faqs.q: Can I get the Certificate III in Asian Cookery through RPL?
faqs.a: Yes, if you have cooked in a commercial Asian kitchen. Photos and videos of your dishes, menus and a reference from your employer are assessed against the units, with practical skills observed.

faqs.q: What's the difference between Asian Cookery and Commercial Cookery?
faqs.a: Both are cook qualifications. Asian Cookery focuses on Asian cuisines, while the Certificate III in Commercial Cookery covers general and Western cookery methods. Choose the one that matches the food you cook.

faqs.q: How long does it take?
faqs.a: Usually 6 to 12 weeks, depending on your evidence and practical assessments.

faqs.q: I learned to cook overseas. Does it count?
faqs.a: Yes. Overseas kitchen experience can be assessed. References, photos and recent Australian kitchen work make your evidence stronger.

faqs.q: What does it cost?
faqs.a: The cost depends on your evidence and any gap training. RPL is usually much cheaper than an apprenticeship. Start with a free eligibility check.

metaTitle: SIT40721 Cert IV in Patisserie RPL — Pastry Chef
metaDescription: Senior pastry chef? Get the SIT40721 Certificate IV in Patisserie through RPL using your experience running a pastry section. Free eligibility check.
heroIntro: The SIT40721 Certificate IV in Patisserie is the qualification for senior pastry chefs who lead a team. If you already run a pastry section, produce showpieces and manage staff and budgets, RPL turns that experience into a nationally recognised qualification.
whoIsItFor:
• Head pastry chefs and pastry sous chefs
  • Senior patissiers in hotels, restaurants and patisseries
  • Patisserie owners
  • Pastry chefs who trained overseas

You'll usually have several years as a pastry chef, including leading staff, rostering, managing a budget and producing advanced work such as chocolate, sugar and marzipan decorations and showpieces.
evidenceExamples:
• Photos and videos of advanced work: showpieces, chocolate and sugar work, entremets
  • Rosters, budgets and ordering records you manage
  • Production plans and recipe costings
  • Training or coaching you've given junior staff
  • A reference from your executive chef or employer
  • Food safety supervisor and food handler certificates
description: The SIT40721 Certificate IV in Patisserie combines advanced pastry skills with kitchen leadership. It covers cakes, pastries, petits fours, desserts and yeast goods, plus marzipan, chocolate confectionery, sugar decorations and sweet showpieces, along with planning cooking operations, managing a budget, rostering, leading people, managing conflict, food safety and WHS.

faqs.q: Can I get the Certificate IV in Patisserie through RPL?
faqs.a: Yes, if you are a senior pastry chef. Photos of your advanced work, rosters, budgets and a reference are assessed against the units, with practical skills observed.

faqs.q: Do I need the Certificate III first?
faqs.a: No, there are no entry requirements. The Certificate IV includes the Certificate III pastry skills, so experienced pastry chefs can go straight to it.

faqs.q: How long does it take?
faqs.a: Usually 6 to 12 weeks.

faqs.q: Do I need a practical assessment?
faqs.a: Usually yes. Your pastry skills are observed in a commercial kitchen or reviewed on recorded video.

faqs.q: What does it cost?
faqs.a: The cost depends on your evidence and any gap training. RPL is usually much cheaper than full study. Start with a free eligibility check.

  • Senior cooks who run a section or a shift
  • Restaurant owners who lead their own kitchen
  • Chefs who trained overseas

You'll usually have several years as a chef, including leading staff, rostering, costing recipes, managing a budget and planning kitchen operations.

metaTitle: SIT60322 Adv Diploma Hospitality Management RPL
metaDescription: Senior hospitality manager? Get the SIT60322 Advanced Diploma of Hospitality Management through RPL using your management experience. Free check.
heroIntro: The SIT60322 Advanced Diploma of Hospitality Management is the senior management qualification for hospitality. If you already manage a venue, hotel department or hospitality business, RPL turns that experience into a nationally recognised qualification.
whoIsItFor:
• Hotel, venue and restaurant general managers
  • Food and beverage managers and department heads
  • Hospitality business owners
  • Multi-site and operations managers

You'll usually have several years in hospitality management, including budgets and finances, business planning, recruiting and leading staff, marketing, legal compliance and WHS systems.
evidenceExamples:
• Budgets, P&L reports and financial plans you're responsible for
  • Business and marketing plans
  • Recruitment, induction and performance records (with names removed)
  • Customer service and quality systems you've set up
  • WHS and compliance documents
  • A reference from the owner, general manager or area manager
description:
The SIT60322 Advanced Diploma of Hospitality Management covers senior management in hospitality: managing organisational finances, budgets and physical assets, developing business plans, managing quality customer service, managing legal risk and compliance, recruiting and leading people, monitoring operations, building business relationships, marketing and running a WHS system.

It sits above the SIT50422 Diploma of Hospitality Management.
searchAliases: advanced diploma of hospitality management rpl

faqs.q: Can I get the Advanced Diploma of Hospitality Management through RPL?
faqs.a: Yes, if you are a senior hospitality manager. Your budgets, plans, staff management records and a senior reference are assessed against the units.

faqs.q: Should I choose the Diploma or the Advanced Diploma?
faqs.a: If you manage a department or a single venue's daily operations, the Diploma usually fits. If you are responsible for finances, business planning and strategy across a business, choose the Advanced Diploma.

faqs.q: How long does it take?
faqs.a: Usually 6 to 12 weeks. It is a large qualification with many units.

faqs.q: Can I do it online?
faqs.a: Mostly. Evidence is submitted online, and your workplace usually confirms your management skills.

faqs.q: What does it cost?
faqs.a: The cost depends on your evidence and any gap training. RPL is usually much cheaper than full study. Start with a free eligibility check.

metaTitle: FBP30521 Cert III in Baking RPL — Baker, Fast Track

heroIntro: The FBP30521 Certificate III in Baking is the trade qualification for bakers. If you already produce bread, pastries, cakes and biscuits in a commercial bakery, RPL recognises your experience so you get the qualification without a full apprenticeship.

  • Bakers who trained overseas

metaTitle: AMP30815 Retail Butcher RPL — Cert III Meat Processing
metaDescription: Experienced butcher? Get the AMP30815 Certificate III in Meat Processing (Retail Butcher) through RPL using your trade experience. Free check.
heroIntro: The AMP30815 Certificate III in Meat Processing (Retail Butcher) is the trade qualification for retail butchers. If you already break down carcases, prepare cuts and serve customers in a butcher shop, RPL recognises your experience so you get the qualification without a full apprenticeship.
whoIsItFor:
• Retail butchers in independent shops and supermarkets
  • Butchers who never finished their apprenticeship
  • Butcher shop owners
  • Butchers who trained overseas

You'll usually have two or more years as a butcher: breaking and boning carcases, preparing specialised and value-added cuts, making sausages, using a bandsaw, serving customers and following hygiene and HACCP rules.
evidenceExamples:
• Photos and videos of your work: breaking, boning, cutting, displays, sausages and value-added products

  • Food safety, HACCP and hygiene records you complete

description: The AMP30815 Certificate III in Meat Processing (Retail Butcher) is the national trade qualification for retail butchers. It covers identifying species and cuts, assessing carcases, breaking and boning, preparing and slicing cuts, preparing specialised cuts, mince, sausages and value-added products, operating a bandsaw, sharpening knives, serving customers and advising on cooking and storage, and following hygiene, quality assurance and HACCP requirements.

faqs.q: Can I get a butcher qualification through RPL?
faqs.a: Yes, if you have worked as a retail butcher. Photos and videos of your work, a reference from your employer and your food safety records are assessed against the units, with practical skills observed.

faqs.q: How long does it take?
faqs.a: Usually 6 to 12 weeks. It is a large qualification, so how complete your evidence is makes a big difference.

faqs.q: Do I need a practical assessment?
faqs.a: Yes. An assessor observes your butchery skills, such as breaking, boning and cutting, in a workplace or on recorded video.

faqs.q: I was a butcher overseas. Can my experience count?
faqs.a: Yes. Overseas butchery experience can be assessed, especially with a reference and recent Australian work.

faqs.q: What does it cost?
faqs.a: The cost depends on your evidence and any gap training. RPL is usually much cheaper than an apprenticeship. Start with a free eligibility check.

metaTitle: AMP40222 Cert IV in Meat Processing RPL — QA & Supervisor
metaDescription: Supervisor or QA officer in meat processing? Get the AMP40222 Certificate IV in Meat Processing through RPL. Free eligibility check.
heroIntro: The AMP40222 Certificate IV in Meat Processing is the qualification for supervisors, quality assurance officers and technical staff in the meat industry. If you already lead teams or run food safety and quality programs in a meat business, RPL turns that experience into a nationally recognised qualification.
whoIsItFor:
• Quality assurance officers and QA managers in meat processing
  • Production supervisors and team leaders
  • Meat inspectors and technical officers
  • Butchery managers with food safety responsibility

You'll usually have several years in the meat industry, including supervising staff or running food safety, quality and good manufacturing practice programs.
evidenceExamples:
• HACCP plans, food safety and quality records you manage
  • Internal audit reports and corrective actions
  • WHS monitoring records and toolbox talks
  • Training you've delivered to staff
  • A reference from your plant manager or employer
description:
The AMP40222 Certificate IV in Meat Processing covers leadership and technical roles in the meat industry: building productive workplace relationships, supporting food safety and quality programs, maintaining good manufacturing practice and monitoring WHS.

Electives cover quality assurance, production supervision, meat safety and related areas. It replaces AMP40415 Certificate IV in Meat Processing (Quality Assurance) and other Certificate IV meat processing qualifications.

faqs.q: Can I get the Certificate IV in Meat Processing through RPL?
faqs.a: Yes, if you supervise or run quality programs in the meat industry. Your HACCP and QA records, audits and a reference are assessed against the units.

faqs.q: What happened to AMP40415 (Quality Assurance)?
faqs.a: It was replaced by AMP40222 Certificate IV in Meat Processing. Quality assurance is now covered through the electives.

faqs.q: How long does it take?

faqs.a: Mostly. Evidence is submitted online, and your workplace confirms your skills.

faqs.a: The cost depends on your evidence and any gap training. RPL is usually much cheaper than full study. Start with a free eligibility check.
